key_insight: In long axisymmetric channels with thin electric double layers, diffusio-osmotic flow is governed strongly by channel geometry: it can be enhanced or suppressed relative to a simple cylinder, while applied pressure adds only an extra independent flow contribution.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a geometry-aware design rule for micro- and nanofluidic devices to tune pumping, hydraulic resistance, and ionic transport using concentration gradients and channel shape.
method: Theory for salt solution flow in long axisymmetric channels driven by concentration and pressure differences.
Thin diffuse-layer approximation with validity retained for large concentration drops.
Comparison of several channel geometries and introduction of an effective-cylinder approximation based on hydrodynamic resistivity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical calculations of flow-rate and pressure-drop curves for several axisymmetric channel shapes, showing nearly linear Δp(Q) relations with slopes that depend sensitively on geometry.
watch_item: The model assumes thin electrostatic diffuse layers and axisymmetric long channels, so accuracy may degrade for strongly non-axisymmetric geometries or cases where the double layer is not thin compared with the local radius.
paper_title: Diffusioosmosis of electrolyte solutions in axisymmetric channels
